protocol_context: M4.0 says the existing hot-water system has existing hot-water boilers with a BACnet interface and that new components shall be integrated into the existing Delta control system.
M4.1 labels a CHILLER SYSTEM INTEGRATION PANEL (BACnet)(E).

control_symbol_legend.quantity_rule: The legend is a symbol key, not an installed-equipment, damper-actuator, or control-valve schedule. Its entries are not counted as field devices.

damper_actuator_schedule.basis: All nine supplied pages were visually reviewed; no dedicated damper-actuator schedule is present. M4.0 contains DA as a legend definition only.

sequences.title: EXISTING HEATING WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION

statements.text: THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHENEVER BOTH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITION EXISTS: OUTSIDE AIR TEMPERATURE DECREASES TO THE HEATING ENABLE SET POINT FOR 10 CONSECUTIVE MINUTES; THERE IS A CALL FOR HEAT FROM AT LEAST ONE ZONE BASED ON A HEATING COIL CONTROL VALVE MINIMUM POSITION OF 25% OPEN FOR 30 CONSECUTIVE SECONDS.

SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD HEATING WATER PUMP; validate running status through the VFD control interface; enable the standby pump on a lead-pump failure and alarm if the standby pump fails to start.

THE DDC CONTROLLER SHALL MODULATE THE VFD BASED ON A DIFFERENTIAL PRESSURE SETPOINT (ADJUSTABLE) LOCATED ACROSS THE PIPING ASSEMBLY; the setpoint is coordinated between balance and control contractors and must allow adequate flow to all hot-water heating coils.
SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE BOILER SYSTEM'S UNIT CONTROLLER; validate through the UCP; on lead-boiler failure enable the lag boiler; alarm if either boiler fails to start.

DDC lead/lag control of heating-water pumps includes monthly lead rotation, manual/operator overrides, and lockout prevention: minimum 10 minutes run and 5 minutes off before restart except for manual or occupied/unoccupied scheduling control.
THE HEATING ENABLE SET POINT SHALL BE SET AT 60°F.

sequences.title: UPDATED CONTROL SEQUENCES ON EXISTING HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHEET

statements.text: EACH BOILER SHALL DISABLE ITS OWN BOILER PUMP RESPECTIVELY.
THE BYPASS CONTROL VALVE (BCV-1) SHALL BE DISABLE AND LOCKED OUT.

EACH BOILER SHALL ENABLE THE RESPECTIVE BOILER PUMP BEFORE FIRING THE BOILER. IF EITHER BOILER PUMP FAILS TO START, THE RESPECTIVE BOILER SHALL NOT ENABLE AND AN ALARM OF THE EVENT SHALL BE SENT TO THE OPERATOR'S WORKSTATION.

WHEN A RUNNING STATUS FROM THE BOILER UNIT CONTROL PANEL (UCP) HAS BEEN CONFIRMED, THE HEATING WATER SYSTEM SHALL CONTINUE TO OPERATE UNDER ITS OWN INTERNAL CONTROLS BY PROVIDING LEAD / LAG SEQUENCING AND ADJUSTING THEIR OWN RAMPING AND LOADING RATES. THE DDC CONTROLLER SHALL SEND THE UNIT CONTROL PANEL A HEATING WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT TO MAINTAIN.

Heating-water supply temperature reset is based on heating-coil-control-valve positions: first enabled maximum 140°F +/- 1°F, decreasing linearly to 100°F while all heating-coil control valves are 90% open or less; it reverses toward maximum when three or more are over 90%, and resets to maximum if one or more reach 100% for 60 consecutive seconds. All stated values are adjustable where printed.

sequences.title: EXISTING CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SEQUENCE OF OPERATION

statements.text: THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE ENABLED WHENEVER ONE OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS EXIST: outside-air temperature rises to the cooling enable set point for 10 consecutive minutes; buffer-tank temperature rises above 45°F for 30 seconds; or there is a call for dehumidification.

SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE AIR-COOLED CHILLER'S UNIT CONTROL PANEL (UCP), validate chiller running status through the UCP, alarm on a failed start, and provide the UCP a chilled-water supply-temperature set point after confirmation.

THE CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHALL BE DISABLED WHENEVER BOTH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS EXIST: outside-air temperature decreases 2° (adjustable) or more below the cooling-enable set point for 10 consecutive minutes (adjustable), and buffer-tank temperature falls below 45°F for 30 seconds.

DDC lead/standby primary-pump control provides automatic rotation by runtime, fixed rotation, or calendar date with manual/operator override. Cooldown disables the chilled-water system 10 minutes before occupied-to-unoccupied switchover of the last air-valve system to use residual cooling capacity in the piping system.
CHILLED WATER SUPPLY TEMPERATURE SET POINT RESET is based on outdoor-air temperature: 60°F outdoor / 55°F supply and 75°F outdoor / 45°F supply, as printed.

sequences.title: UPDATED CONTROL SEQUENCES ON EXISTING CHILLED WATER SYSTEM SHEET

statements.text: SEND AN ENABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP; validate running status through the current sensing relay; if the lead pump fails to start, enable the standby pump; if the standby pump fails to start, alarm the operator's workstation.

SEND A DISABLE COMMAND TO THE LEAD CHILLED WATER PUMP. When the chilled-water system is disabled, the lead primary chilled-water pump continues for 10 consecutive minutes; validate running status through the current sensing relay and alarm if the pump fails to stop.

sensor_and_zone_ledger.physical_count_scope: The supplied plans/schedules do not map space sensors, CO2 sensors, or smart thermostats to zones. Schematic transmitter symbols are not converted to plan-installed device counts.
